FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Rubber Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. The concerned committee has decided to prepare common methods of test for synthetic rubber under SR ( Synthetic Rubber ) series. namely, IS 11720 and this will be applicable to all types of synthetic This standard ( Part 3 ) is the third in the series. The other rubbers being produced indigenously. standards of this series are as follows: Part 1 Methods of test for synthetic rubber: Part 1 Determination of antioxidants Part 2 Methods of test for synthetic rubber: Part 2 Measurement of vulcanization with oscillating disc curemeter ( SR : 2 ) ( SR : 1 ); and characteristics

In preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IS0 289 : 1985 `Rubber, unvulcanized -- Determination of mooney viscosity' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the fkal value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 bRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

Indian Standard METHODS OF TEST FOR SYNTHETIC RUBBER
PART 1 SCOPE 3 DETERMINATION OF MOONEY VISCOSITY

3 OUTLINE

OF THE METHOD

I.1 This standard ( Part 3 ) prescribes method for measuring the mooney viscosity of uncompounded or compounded synthetic rubbers by use of the shearing disk viscometer. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to this standard: Title IS No. Methods of test for natural 3660, of ( Part 1 ) : 1972 rubber : Determination ash, total copper, manganese, rubber hydrocarbon, viscosity ( shearing disk visomixing and meter ), and of rubber in vulcanizing standard compo,und ( first
revision ) 5599 : 1970

3.1 The torque which has to be applied under specified conditions in order to rotate a metal dtsk in a cylindrical chamber formed from mating dies filled with rubber is measured. The resistance to this rotation, offered by the rubber, is expressed in arbitrary units as the Mooney viscosity of the test piece. 4 APPARATUS

4.1.2 Dies The two dies forming the cavity shall be formed from non-deforming unplated hardened steel of minimum Rockwell hardness HRC 60. The dimensions of the cavity are given in Fig. 1 and shall be measured from the highest surfaces. For good heat transfer each die should preferably be made from only one piece of steel. The surfaces shall have radial V-grooves on the flat surface to prevent slipping. The grooves shall be spaced radially at 20" intervals and shall extend from an outer circle of diameter 47 mm to an inner circle of diameter 7 mm for the upper die and to within I.5 mm of the hole in the lower die; each groove shall form a 90" angle in the die surface with the bisector of the angle perpendicular to the surface and shall be
1.0 & 0.1 mm wide at the surface ( see Fig. 2 ).

rotor

4.1.1.1 It is permissible to use a smaller rotor where high viscosity makes this necessary. This small rotor should have the same dimensions as the large rotor except that the diameter should be 30.48 f O-03 mm. Results obtained with the small rotor are not identical with those obtained using the large rotor.

each die may be formed from two pie'ces of steel with rectangular section grooves on the surfaces to prevent slipping. The flat surfaces of the dies have two sets of these grooves at right angles to each other ( see Fig. 3 ).

of maintaining the temperature of the platens and that of the dies to within f 0*5"C of the test temperature. After insertion of the sample the devices shall be capable of returning the temperature of the dies to within & 0.W of the test temperature within 5 minutes. 4.1.5 Temperature Measurement The test temperature is defined as the steady state temperature of the closed dies with the rotor in place and the cavity empty. A temperature sensor shall be present in each die for measurement of die temperature. The sensor shall be located for the best possible heat contact with the dies, that is, heat gaps and other heat resistance shall be excluded. The axes of the sensors shall be at a distance of 3 to 5 mm from the working surface of the dies and 15 to 20 mm from the rotation axis of the rotor. The temperature measuring system shall be capable of indicating temperature to an accuracy of 0*25"C!.

results.

The two types of die may not give the same

The dies may be closed and held closed by hydraulic, pneumatic or mechnical means. A force of 11.5 f 0.5 kN shall be maintained on the dies during the test.

3 GROOVBS WITH RECTANGULAR SECTIONOF DIE AND ROTOR

4.1.3 Rotor The rotor shall be fabricated from a nondeforming unplated hardened steel of minimum Rockwell hardness HRC 60. The rotor surfaces should be grooved as in the manner shown in Fig. 3. The rotor is fastened at right angles to a shaft having a diameter 10 f 1 mm and of length such that in the closed die cavity the clearance above the rotor does not differ from that below by more than 0.25 mm. The rotor shaft shall bear on the spindle which turns the rotor shaft, not on the wall of the die cavity. The clearance at the point where the rotor enters the cavity should be small enough to prevent rubber leaving the cavity. A grommet, O-ring or other sealing device may be used as a seal at this point. or runout of the rotor while turning in the viscometer shall not exceed O-1 mm. The relative speed of rotation between the rotor and dies shall be O-209 rt. 4.1.6.1 For all types of closing devices, a piece of soft tissue paper not thicker than 0.04 mm placed between the mating surfaces should show a continuous pattern of uniform intensity when the dies are closed. A non-uniform pattern indicates incorrect adjustment of die closure, worn or faulty mating surfaces or distortion of dies; any of these conditions result in leakage and erroneouS resu1ts* 4.1.7 Torque Measurement and Calibration The torque required to turn the rotor is recorded or indicated on a linear scale graduated in Mooney units. The reading shall be zero when the machine is run empty and 100 f 0.5 when a torque of 8.30 f 0.02 Nm is applied to the rotor shaft. Therefore, torque of O-083 Nm is equivalent to 1 Mooney units. The scale shall be capable of being read to 0.5 Mooney units. Variation from zero shall be less than & 0.5 Mooney units when the machine is running with the rotor in place, and the dies closed and empty.

shall be calibrated while the machine is running at the test temperature. A suitable method for the calibration of most machines is as follows: The scale is calibrated by applying certified masses fastened with flexible wire of diameter 0.45 mm to an appropriate rotor. During calibration the rotor is turned at 0.029 rad/ seconds and the platens are at the specified test temperature. hole in the test piece and place the rotor in the viscometer. Place the second test piece centrally on the rotor and close the dies as quickly as possible.

5.1.2 The test piece shall consist of two disks of rubber, of diameter about 50 mm and of thick6 mm, sufficient to fill ness approximately ,completely the die cavity of the viscometer. The rubber disks shall be as free as possible from air and from pockets that may trap air against the rotor and die surfaces. 8.2 Precision 8.2.1 Repeatability For the range of viscosity from 40 to 60 Mooney units, the standard deviation of repeatability same operator, apparatus, same ( same laboratory and short intervals of time ) of a uniform sample of rubber is about O-2 Mooney units. Variation in sample preparation results in standard deviation of about 1 Mooney unit. The standard deviation of repeatability with increasing viscosity. The use of test pieces of the standard decreases repeatability. increases

8.2.2 Reproducibility For the range of viscosity from 40 to 60 Mooney units, the standard deviation of reproducibility ( different operator, different apparatus of sample design, different laboratories the different times ) of a uniform and/or sample of rubber is up to 2 Mooney units. In special cases variability among laboratories may cause even larger variations in results. Part of the interlaboratory variability is due to sample preparation, and part to differences in calibrating or adjusting the viscometer. The standard deviation of reproducibility increases with increasing viscosity. The use of test piece of constant volume decreases the standard deviation of reproducibility. 5

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard.
